\section*{AP \({ }^{\text {® }}\) CALCULUS AB \\ 2012 SCORING GUIDELINES}

\section*{Question 5}

The rate at which a baby bird gains weight is proportional to the difference between its adult weight and its current weight. At time \(t=0\), when the bird is first weighed, its weight is 20 grams. If \(B(t)\) is the weight of the bird, in grams, at time \(t\) days after it is first weighed, then
\[
\frac{d B}{d t}=\frac{1}{5}(100-B) .
\]
Let \(y=B(t)\) be the solution to the differential equation above with initial condition \(B(0)=20\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Is the bird gaining weight faster when it weighs 40 grams or when it weighs 70 grams? Explain your reasoning.
\item[(b)] Find \(\frac{d^{2} B}{d t^{2}}\) in terms of \(B\). Use \(\frac{d^{2} B}{d t^{2}}\) to explain why the graph of \(B\) cannot resemble the following graph.
\item[(c)] Use separation of variables to find \(y=B(t)\), the particular solution to the differential equation with initial condition \(B(0)=20\).
\end{itemize}
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/6816bd3b-1f36-4adc-8ba5-e80bf25c3a04-1.jpg?height=445&width=516&top_left_y=737&top_left_x=1414)
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] \(\left.\frac{d B}{d t}\right|_{B=40}=\frac{1}{5}(60)=12\)
\[
\left.\frac{d B}{d t}\right|_{B=70}=\frac{1}{5}(30)=6
\]
Because \(\left.\frac{d B}{d t}\right|_{B=40}>\left.\frac{d B}{d t}\right|_{B=70}\), the bird is gaining weight faster when it weighs 40 grams.
\item[(b)] \(\frac{d^{2} B}{d t^{2}}=-\frac{1}{5} \frac{d B}{d t}=-\frac{1}{5} \cdot \frac{1}{5}(100-B)=-\frac{1}{25}(100-B)\) Therefore, the graph of \(B\) is concave down for \(20 \leq B<100\). A portion of the given graph is concave up.
\item[(c)] \(\frac{d B}{d t}=\frac{1}{5}(100-B)\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \int \frac{1}{100-B} d B=\int \frac{1}{5} d t \\
& -\ln |100-B|=\frac{1}{5} t+C
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(20 \leq B<100,|100-B|=100-B\).
\[
\begin{aligned}
& -\ln (100-20)=\frac{1}{5}(0)+C \Rightarrow-\ln (80)=C \\
& 100-B=80 e^{-t / 5} \\
& B(t)=100-80 e^{-t / 5}, \quad t \geq 0
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
